questions.text: Let R be a relation defined over N, where N is set of natural numbers, defined as \"mRn if and only if m is a multiple of n, m, n $\in$ N.\" Find whether R is reflexive, symmetric and transitive or not.

answer.text: R on N: mRn ⇔ m is a multiple of n. Reflexive: every x is a multiple of itself ⇒ xRx. Not symmetric: 8 is a multiple of 2 (8R2) but 2 is not a multiple of 8. Transitive: x = my, y = nz ⇒ x = (mn)z, so xRz. Hence R is reflexive and transitive but not symmetric.

Check if the relation thus formed is reflexive, symmetric and transitive or not. Hence, state whether it is an equivalence relation or not.

answer.text: Relation R = {(x,y): 2x + y = 41, x,y ∈ N} = {(1,39),(2,37),…,(20,1)}. Domain = {1,2,…,20}, Range = {1,3,5,…,39}. (1,1) ∉ R ⇒ not reflexive. (1,39) ∈ R but (39,1) ∉ R ⇒ not symmetric. (11,19),(19,3) ∈ R but (11,3) ∉ R ⇒ not transitive. Hence R is not an equivalence relation.

questions.text: Show that the function $f : N \to N$, where N is a set of natural numbers, given by $f(n) = \begin{cases} n - 1, & \text{if n is even} \\ n + 1, & \text{if n is odd} \end{cases}$ is a bijection.

answer.text: f: N→N, f(n) = n−1 if n even, n+1 if n odd. One-one: if f(x) = f(y) with x, y same parity then x±1 = y±1 ⇒ x = y; opposite parity is impossible (odd and even cannot differ by 2). Onto: for any y ∈ N, if y is odd take x = y+1 (even), if y is even take x = y−1 (odd), giving f(x) = y. Hence f is a bijection.

questions.text: Let $f : A \to B$ be defined by $f(x) = \dfrac{x - 2}{x - 3}$, where $A = \mathbb{R} - \{3\}$ and $B = \mathbb{R} - \{1\}$. Discuss the bijectivity of the function.

answer.text: f(x) = (x−2)/(x−3), A = R−{3}, B = R−{1}. One-one: f(x₁) = f(x₂) ⇒ (x₁−2)(x₂−3) = (x₂−2)(x₁−3) ⇒ x₁ = x₂. Onto: for y ∈ B, x = (3y−2)/(y−1) ∈ A gives f(x) = y. Hence f is one-one and onto, i.e. bijective.

questions.text: Show that the function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ defined by $f(x) = 4x^3 - 5$, $\forall\,x \in \mathbb{R}$ is one-one and onto.

answer.text: f: R→R, f(x) = 4x³ − 5. One-one: f(x₁) = f(x₂) ⇒ x₁³ = x₂³ ⇒ x₁ = x₂. Onto: for y ∈ R, x = ((y+5)/4)^{1/3} ∈ R gives f(x) = y. Hence f is one-one and onto (bijective).

questions.text: Let R be a relation defined on a set N of natural numbers such that $R = \{(x, y) : xy \text{ is a square of a natural number}, x, y \in N\}$. Determine if the relation R is an equivalence relation.

answer.text: R on N: x R y iff xy is a perfect square. Reflexive: x·x = x² is a perfect square ⇒ (x,x) ∈ R. Symmetric: xy perfect square ⇒ yx perfect square. Transitive: if xy and yz are perfect squares, then xy·yz = xz·y² is a perfect square ⇒ xz is a perfect square ⇒ (x,z) ∈ R. Hence R is an equivalence relation.

questions.text: A relation R is defined on Z, the set of integers, as $R = \{(x, y) : |x - y| \text{ is divisible by a prime number '}p\text{'}, x, y \in Z\}$. Check whether R is an equivalence relation or not.

answer.text: R on Z: (x,y) ∈ R iff |x−y| is divisible by a prime p. Reflexive: |x−x| = 0 is divisible by p ⇒ (x,x) ∈ R. Symmetric: |x−y| = |y−x| ⇒ (y,x) ∈ R. Transitive: if |x−y| and |y−z| are divisible by p, then (x−y)+(y−z) = x−z is divisible by p ⇒ |x−z| divisible ⇒ (x,z) ∈ R. Hence R is reflexive, symmetric and transitive — an equivalence relation.

questions.text: A function $f : \mathbb{R} - \left\{\dfrac{3}{5}\right\} \to \mathbb{R} - \left\{\dfrac{3}{5}\right\}$ is defined as $f(x) = \dfrac{3x + 2}{5x - 3}$. Show that $f$ is one-one and onto.

answer.text: f: R−{3/5} → R−{3/5}, f(x) = (3x+2)/(5x−3). One-one: f(x₁) = f(x₂) ⇒ (3x₁+2)(5x₂−3) = (3x₂+2)(5x₁−3) ⇒ x₁ = x₂. Onto: for any y in the codomain, x = (3y+2)/(5y−3) lies in the domain and f(x) = y. Hence f is one-one and onto (bijective).

questions.text: Show that $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ defined as $f(x) = \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1 + x^2}}$ is one-one but not onto.

answer.text: f(x) = x/√(1+x²). One-one: f(x₁) = f(x₂) ⇒ x₁²(1+x₂²) = x₂²(1+x₁²) ⇒ x₁² = x₂² ⇒ x₁ = x₂ (both same sign, rejecting x₁ = −x₂). Not onto: y = x/√(1+x²) ⇒ x = ±√(y²/(1−y²)), defined only for y ∈ (−1,1) ⇒ range = (−1,1) ≠ R (codomain). Hence f is one-one but not onto.

questions.text: Let $n$ be a fixed positive integer. A relation R is defined in set Z such that $R = \{(x, y) : (x - y) \text{ is divisible by } n,\ \forall\, x, y \in Z\}$. Determine if R is an equivalence relation.

answer.text: R = {(x,y): (x−y) divisible by n} on Z. Reflexive: x−x = 0 is divisible by n. Symmetric: x−y = np ⇒ y−x = n(−p) divisible by n. Transitive: x−y = np, y−z = nr ⇒ x−z = n(p+r) divisible by n. Hence R is an equivalence relation.

answer.text: Set A = {G₁,G₂,G₃,G₄} (n=4), Set B = {B₁,B₂,B₃} (n=3). (i) Number of relations A→B = 2^{4×3} = 2¹² = 4096. questions.text: Differentiate $2^{\cos^2 x}$ w.r.t. $\cos^2 x$.

answer.text: Let u = 2^{cos²x} ⇒ du/dx = 2^{cos²x}(−2 cos x sin x)log 2; v = cos²x ⇒ dv/dx = −2 cos x sin x. Hence du/dv = (du/dx)/(dv/dx) = 2^{cos²x} log 2.

questions.text: If $\tan^{-1}(x^2 + y^2) = a^2$, then find $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$.

answer.text: tan⁻¹(x² + y²) = a² ⇒ x² + y² = tan a² (a constant). Differentiating both sides w.r.t. x: 2x + 2y·dy/dx = 0 ⇒ dy/dx = −x/y.

questions.text: If $\sqrt{1 - x^2} + \sqrt{1 - y^2} = a(x - y)$, then show that $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1 - y^2}{1 - x^2}}$.

answer.text: √(1−x²) + √(1−y²) = a(x−y). Put x = sin A, y = sin B ⇒ cos A + cos B = a(sin A − sin B) ⇒ 2cos((A+B)/2)cos((A−B)/2) = 2a cos((A+B)/2)sin((A−B)/2) ⇒ cot((A−B)/2) = a ⇒ A − B = 2cot⁻¹a ⇒ sin⁻¹x − sin⁻¹y = 2cot⁻¹a. Differentiating: 1/√(1−x²) − (1/√(1−y²))dy/dx = 0 ⇒ dy/dx = √((1−y²)/(1−x²)).

questions.text: If $x = a\left(\cos\theta + \log\tan\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)$ and $y = a\sin\theta$, then find $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$ at $\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$.

answer.text: x = a(cos θ + log tan(θ/2)) ⇒ dx/dθ = a(−sin θ + 1/sin θ) = a cos θ cot θ... = a cot θ cos θ; y = sin θ ⇒ dy/dθ = cos θ. dy/dx = tan θ/a. d²y/dx² = (sec²θ/a)(dθ/dx) = sec³θ tan θ/a². At θ = π/4: = (√2)³·1/a² = 2√2/a².

If $x = e^{x/y}$, then prove that $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x - y}{x\log x}$.

answer.text: x = e^{x/y} ⇒ log x = x/y ⇒ y log x = x. Differentiating w.r.t. x: y/x + log x·dy/dx = 1 ⇒ dy/dx = (1 − y/x)/log x = (x − y)/(x log x).

questions.text: If $f(x) = \begin{cases} 2x - 3, & -3 \leq x \leq -2 \\ x + 1, & -2 < x \leq 0 \end{cases}$. Check the differentiability of $f(x)$ at $x = -2$.

answer.text: f(x) = 2x − 3 for −3 ≤ x ≤ −2, and x + 1 for −2 < x ≤ 0; f(−2) = −7. LHD at x = −2 = lim_{h→0}[2(−2−h)−3−(−7)]/(−h) = 2. RHD = lim_{h→0}[(−2+h+1)−(−7)]/h = lim (6+h)/h, which does not exist. Since RHD does not exist, f is not differentiable at x = −2.

questions.text: If $y = \log\left(\sqrt{x} + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\right)^2$, then show that $x(x + 1)^2 y_2 + (x + 1)^2 y_1 = 2$.

answer.text: y = log(√x + 1/√x)² = 2log(x+1) − log x. y₁ = 2/(x+1) − 1/x = (x−1)/(x(x+1)) ⇒ (x+1)y₁ = 1 − 1/x. Differentiating: (x+1)y₂ + y₁ = 1/x² ⇒ multiplying by x(x+1): x(x+1)²y₂ + x(x+1)y₁ = 1 + 1/x = 1 + 1 − (x+1)y₁ ⇒ x(x+1)²y₂ + (x+1)²y₁ = 2.

questions.text: If $x\sqrt{1 + y} + y\sqrt{1 + x} = 0$, $-1 < x < 1$, $x \neq y$, then prove that $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{-1}{(1 + x)^2}$.

answer.text: x√(1+y) + y√(1+x) = 0 ⇒ x√(1+y) = −y√(1+x) ⇒ x²(1+y) = y²(1+x) ⇒ (x−y)(x+y) + xy(x−y) = 0 ⇒ (x−y)(x+y+xy) = 0. Since x ≠ y, x + y + xy = 0 ⇒ y = −x/(1+x). Differentiating: dy/dx = −1/(1+x)².

questions.text: If $y = 5\cos x - 3\sin x$, prove that $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + y = 0$.

answer.text: y = 5cos x − 3sin x. dy/dx = −5sin x − 3cos x; d²y/dx² = −5cos x + 3sin x = −(5cos x − 3sin x) = −y. Hence d²y/dx² + y = 0.

questions.text: For a positive constant '$a$', differentiate $a^{t + \frac{1}{t}}$ with respect to $\left(t + \dfrac{1}{t}\right)^a$, where $t$ is a non-zero real number.

answer.text: Differentiate u = a^{t+1/t} w.r.t. v = (t+1/t)^a. du/dt = a^{t+1/t}·log a·(1 − 1/t²); dv/dt = a(t+1/t)^{a−1}·(1 − 1/t²). du/dv = (du/dt)/(dv/dt) = a^{t+1/t}·log a / [a(t + 1/t)^{a−1}].

questions.text: Find $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ if $y^x + x^y + x^x = a^b$, where $a$ and $b$ are constants.

answer.text: y^x + x^y + x^x = a^b (constant). Let u = y^x, v = x^y, w = x^x. Logarithmic differentiation: du/dx = xy^{x−1}·y′ + y^x log y; dv/dx = yx^{y−1} + x^y log x·y′; dw/dx = x^x(1 + log x). Since du/dx + dv/dx + dw/dx = 0, dy/dx = −[x^x(1 + log x) + y^x log y + yx^{y−1}] / [x·y^{x−1} + x^y log x].

questions.text: If $-2x^2 - 5xy + y^3 = 76$, then find $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$.

answer.text: −2x² − 5xy + y³ = 76. Differentiating: −4x − 5y − 5x·y′ + 3y²·y′ = 0 ⇒ y′(3y² − 5x) = 4x + 5y ⇒ dy/dx = (4x + 5y)/(3y² − 5x).

Check whether function $f(x)$ defined as $f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{|x - 3|}{2(x - 3)}, & x < 3 \\ \dfrac{x - 6}{6}, & x \geq 3 \end{cases}$ is continuous at $x = 3$ or not.

answer.text: Continuity at x = 3: for x < 3, |x−3|/(2(x−3)) = −1/2, and for x ≥ 3, f(x) = (x−6)/6. So f(3) = −1/2, LHL = lim_{x→3⁻} (−1/2) = −1/2, RHL = lim_{x→3⁺}(x−6)/6 = −1/2. Since LHL = RHL = f(3) = −1/2, f is continuous at x = 3.

questions.text: If $\sqrt{3}(x^2 + y^2) = 4xy$, then find $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ at $\left(\dfrac{1}{2}, \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$.

answer.text: √3(x²+y²) = 4xy ⇒ differentiating both sides w.r.t x: √3(2x + 2y·dy/dx) = 4(x·dy/dx + y) ⇒ dy/dx = (2y − √3x)/(√3y − 2x); at (1/2, √3/2), dy/dx = √3.

questions.text: If $x = \cos t$, $y = \cos mt$, prove that $(1 - x^2)\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} - x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + m^2 y = 0$.

answer.text: x = cos t, y = cos mt ⇒ dx/dt = −sin t, dy/dt = −m sin mt ⇒ dy/dx = (m sin mt)/sin t, i.e. sin t·(dy/dx) = m sin mt. questions.text: The absolute maximum value of function $f(x) = x^3 - 3x + 2$ in $[0, 2]$ is :
Find the intervals in which function $f(x) = 5x^{3/2} - 3x^{5/2}$ is (i) increasing (ii) decreasing.

answer.text: f(x) = 5x^{3/2} − 3x^{5/2} ⇒ f′(x) = (15/2)√x(1 − x). f′(x) = 0 ⇒ x = 0, 1. (i) For x ∈ [0,1], f′(x) ≥ 0, so f is increasing on [0,1]. (ii) For x ∈ [1,∞), f′(x) ≤ 0, so f is decreasing on [1, ∞).

questions.text: Each side of an equilateral triangle is increasing at the rate of 3 cm/s. At what rate is area increasing when the side of the triangle is 15 cm ?

answer.text: Equilateral triangle side a, da/dt = 3 cm/s. Area A = (√3/4)a² ⇒ dA/dt = (√3 a/2)·da/dt. At a = 15: dA/dt = (√3·15/2)·3 = 45√3/2 cm²/s.

questions.text: Find the absolute maximum and absolute minimum of function $f(x) = 2x^3 - 15x^2 + 36x + 1$ on $[1, 5]$.

answer.text: f(x) = 2x³ − 15x² + 36x + 1 on [1,5]. f′(x) = 6(x²−5x+6) = 6(x−2)(x−3) = 0 ⇒ x = 2, 3 ∈ [1,5]. f(1) = 24, f(2) = 29, f(3) = 28, f(5) = 56. Absolute maximum value = 56 (at x = 5); absolute minimum value = 24 (at x = 1).

questions.text: A technical company is designing a rectangular solar panel installation on a roof using 300 metres of boundary material. The design includes a partition running parallel to one of the sides dividing the area (roof) into two sections. Let the length of the side perpendicular to the partition be $x$ metres and with parallel to the partition be $y$ metres. On the basis of the above information, answer the following questions : (i) Write the equation for the total boundary material used in the boundary and parallel to the partition in terms of $x$ and $y$. (ii) Write the area of the solar panel as a function of $x$. (iii)(a) Find the critical points of the area function. Use second derivative test to determine critical points at the maximum area. Also, find the maximum area.  OR  (iii)(b) Using first derivative test, calculate the maximum area the company can enclose with the 300 metres of boundary material, considering the parallel partition.

answer.text: Rectangular panel, 300 m boundary + one partition parallel to a side; perpendicular side x, parallel side y. (i) 2x + 3y = 300. (ii) A = xy = (x/3)(300 − 2x) = (1/3)(300x − 2x²). (iii)(a) dA/dx = (1/3)(300 − 4x) = 0 ⇒ x = 75; d²A/dx² = −4/3 < 0 ⇒ maximum; maximum area = (75/3)(300 − 150) = 3750 m². [OR (iii)(b) By the first-derivative test dA/dx changes + → − at x = 75 ⇒ maximum; maximum area = 3750 m².]

questions.text: A cylindrical tank of radius 10 cm is being filled with sugar at the rate of $100\pi\ \text{cm}^3/\text{s}$. The rate, at which the height of the sugar inside the tank is increasing, is :

answer.text: $1$ cm/s

questions.text: Find the values of '$a$' for which $f(x) = \sin x - ax + b$ is increasing on $\mathbb{R}$.

answer.text: f(x) = sin x − ax + b. f′(x) = cos x − a. For f increasing on R, f′(x) ≥ 0 ⇒ a ≤ cos x for all x. Since −1 ≤ cos x ≤ 1, this requires a ≤ −1. Hence a ∈ (−∞, −1].

questions.text: A small town is analyzing the pattern of a new street light installation. The lights are set up in such a way that the intensity of light at any point $x$ metres from the start of the street can be modelled by $f(x) = e^x\sin x$, where $x$ is in metres. Based on the above, answer the following : (i) Find the intervals on which the $f(x)$ is increasing or decreasing, $x \in [0, \pi]$. (ii) Verify, whether each critical point when $x \in [0, \pi]$ is a point of local maximum or local minimum or a point of inflexion.

answer.text: Intensity f(x) = eˣ sin x on [0, π]. (i) f′(x) = eˣ(cos x + sin x) = 0 ⇒ cos x = −sin x ⇒ x = 3π/4. f′(x) ≥ 0 on [0, 3π/4] (increasing) and f′(x) ≤ 0 on [3π/4, π] (decreasing). (ii) f″(x) = 2eˣ cos x; f″(3π/4) < 0, so x = 3π/4 is a point of local maximum.

questions.text: The values of $\lambda$, so that $f(x) = \sin x - \cos x - \lambda x + C$ decreases for all real values of $x$ are :

answer.text: $\lambda \geq \sqrt{2}$

questions.text: If $f(x) = 2x + \cos x$, then $f(x)$ :

answer.text: is an increasing function

questions.text: Find the least value of '$a$' so that $f(x) = 2x^2 - ax + 3$ is an increasing function on $[2, 4]$.

answer.text: f(x) = 2x² − ax + 3 ⇒ f′(x) = 4x − a. On [2,4], 8 − a ≤ 4x − a ≤ 16 − a. For f increasing, f′(x) ≥ 0 ⇒ 8 − a ≥ 0 ⇒ a ≤ 8. Since a can be any value ≤ 8, the least value of a does not exist.

questions.text: If $f(x) = x + \dfrac{1}{x}$, $x \geq 1$, show that $f$ is an increasing function.

answer.text: f(x) = x + 1/x, x ≥ 1 ⇒ f′(x) = 1 − 1/x² = (x²−1)/x². For x ≥ 1, (x²−1)/x² ≥ 0 ⇒ f′(x) ≥ 0, so f is an increasing function.

questions.text: For the curve $y = 5x - 2x^3$, if $x$ increases at the rate of 2 units/s, then how fast is the slope of the curve changing when $x = 2$ ?

answer.text: y = 5x − 2x³, dx/dt = 2 units/s. Slope m = dy/dx = 5 − 6x² ⇒ dm/dt = −12x·dx/dt = −24x. At x = 2, dm/dt = −24(2) = −48. Hence the slope of the curve is decreasing at the rate of 48 units/s.

questions.text: The relation between the height of the plant ($y$ cm) with respect to exposure to sunlight is governed by the equation $y = 4x - \dfrac{1}{2}x^2$, where $x$ is the number of days exposed to sunlight. (i) Find the rate of growth of the plant with respect to sunlight. (ii) In how many days will the plant attain its maximum height ? What is the maximum height ?

answer.text: Plant height y = 4x − ½x² (x = days of sunlight). (i) Rate of growth dy/dx = 4 − x cm/day. (ii) For maximum height dy/dx = 0 ⇒ x = 4 days; d²y/dx² = −1 < 0 confirms a maximum. Maximum height = y(4) = 16 − ½(16) = 8 cm.

questions.text: The slope of the curve $y = -x^3 + 3x^2 + 8x - 20$ is maximum at :

Surface area of a balloon (spherical), when air is blown into it, increases at a rate of $5\ \text{mm}^2/\text{s}$. When the radius of the balloon is 8 mm, find the rate at which the volume of the balloon is increasing.

answer.text: Spherical balloon, dS/dt = 5 mm²/s, find dV/dt at r = 8. S = 4πr² ⇒ dS/dt = 8πr·dr/dt ⇒ dr/dt = 5/(8πr). V = (4/3)πr³ ⇒ dV/dt = 4πr²·dr/dt = (5/2)r. At r = 8, dV/dt = 20 mm³/s.

questions.text: Find the value of '$a$' for which $f(x) = \sqrt{3}\sin x - \cos x - 2ax + 6$ is decreasing in $\mathbb{R}$.

answer.text: f(x) = √3 sin x − cos x − 2ax + 6 decreasing on R ⇒ f′(x) ≤ 0 for all x. f′(x) = √3 cos x + sin x − 2a = 2(cos(x − π/6)) − 2a ≤ 0 ⇒ a ≥ cos(x − π/6) for all x. Since max of cos(x − π/6) = 1, a ≥ 1, i.e. a ∈ [1, ∞).

questions.text: A carpenter needs to make a wooden cuboidal box, closed from all sides, which has a square base and fixed volume. Since he is short of the paint required to paint the box on completion, he wants the surface area to be minimum. On the basis of the above information, answer the following questions : (i) Taking length = breadth = $x$ m and height = $y$ m, express the surface area (S) of the box in terms of $x$ and its volume (V), which is constant. (ii) Find $\dfrac{dS}{dx}$. (iii)(a) Find a relation between $x$ and $y$ such that the surface area (S) is minimum.  OR  (iii)(b) If surface area (S) is constant, the volume $(V) = \dfrac{1}{4}(Sx - 2x^3)$, $x$ being the edge of base. Show that volume (V) is maximum for $x = \sqrt{\dfrac{S}{6}}$.

answer.text: Closed cuboidal box, square base side x, height y, fixed volume V = x²y. (i) y = V/x², S = 2x² + 4xy = 2x² + 4V/x. (ii) dS/dx = 4x − 4V/x² = 4(x − V/x²). (iii)(a) dS/dx = 0 ⇒ V = x³ ⇒ x²y = x³ ⇒ y = x; d²S/dx² = 4(1 + 2V/x³) > 0, so S is minimum when y = x (a cube). [OR (iii)(b) V = (1/4)(Sx − 2x³); dV/dx = (1/4)(S − 6x²) = 0 ⇒ x = √(S/6); d²V/dx² = −3x < 0 at x = √(S/6), so volume is maximum for x = √(S/6).]

questions.text: Determine the values of $x$ for which $f(x) = \dfrac{x - 4}{x + 1}$, $x \neq -1$ is an increasing or a decreasing function.

answer.text: f(x) = (x−4)/(x+1), x ≠ −1. f′(x) = [(x+1) − (x−4)]/(x+1)² = 5/(x+1)² > 0 for all x ≠ −1. Hence f is increasing throughout its domain R − {−1}.

questions.text: A ladder of fixed length '$h$' is to be placed along the wall such that it is free to move along the height of the wall. Based upon the above information, answer the following questions : (i) Express the distance ($y$) between the wall and foot of the ladder in terms of '$h$' and height ($x$) on the wall at a certain instant. Also, write an expression in terms of $h$ and $x$ for the area (A) of the right triangle, as seen from the side by an observer. (ii) Find the derivative of the area (A) with respect to the height on the wall ($x$), and find its critical point. (iii)(a) Show that the area (A) of the right triangle is maximum at the critical point.  OR  (iii)(b) If the foot of the ladder whose length is 5 m, is being pulled towards the wall such that the rate of decrease of distance ($y$) is 2 m/s, then at what rate is the height on the wall ($x$) increasing, when the foot of the ladder is 3 m away from the wall ?

answer.text: Ladder of fixed length h; height on wall x, distance of foot from wall y. (i) y² = h² − x² ⇒ y = √(h²−x²); Area A = ½xy = ½x√(h²−x²). (ii) dA/dx = ½√(h²−x²) − x²/(2√(h²−x²)); dA/dx = 0 ⇒ x = h/√2 (critical point). (iii)(a) A″ < 0 at x = h/√2, so A is maximum at the critical point. [OR (iii)(b) h = 5, y = 3 ⇒ x = 4. From y² = 25 − x²: 2y·dy/dt = −2x·dx/dt; with dy/dt = −2 m/s, 2(3)(−2) = −2(4)dx/dt ⇒ dx/dt = 1.5 m/s (height increasing at 1.5 m/s).]

questions.text: A spherical ball has a variable diameter $\dfrac{5}{2}(3x + 1)$. The rate of change of its volume w.r.t. $x$, when $x = 1$, is :
If $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is defined as $f(x) = 3x - \sin x$, then $f$ is :

answer.text: an increasing function

questions.text: Amongst all pairs of positive integers with product as 289, find which of the two numbers add up to the least.

answer.text: Numbers x, y with xy = 289 ⇒ y = 289/x. Sum S = x + 289/x. dS/dx = 1 − 289/x² = 0 ⇒ x = 17 (positive). d²S/dx² = 578/x³ > 0 at x = 17, so S is minimum. Thus x = 17, y = 17 add up to the least sum (= 34).

questions.text: The least value of $f(x) = x^3 - 12x$, $x \in [0, 3]$ is :

A room freshner bottle in the shape of an inverted cone sprays the perfume at regular intervals such that volume of the perfume in the bottle decreases at the steady rate of $1\ \text{mm}^3/\text{min}$. Find the rate at which level of perfume is dropping at an instant when level of perfume in the bottle is 10 mm, if the semi-vertical angle of conical bottle is $\dfrac{\pi}{6}$.

answer.text: Inverted cone, semi-vertical angle π/6 ⇒ r/h = tan(π/6) = 1/√3, so r = h/√3 and V = (1/3)πr²h = πh³/9. Given dV/dt = −1 mm³/min = (π/3)h²·dh/dt ⇒ dh/dt = −3/(πh²); at h = 10 mm, dh/dt = −3/(100π). The perfume level is dropping at 3/(100π) mm/min.

questions.text: An online delivery company running in a city has 5000 subscribers and collects annual subscription fees of Rs. 300 per subscriber for unlimited free deliveries. The company wishes to increase the annual subscription fee. It is predicted that, for every increase of Rs. 1, ten subscribers will discontinue. Assume that the company increased the annual fee by Rs. $x$. Based on the given information, answer the following questions : (i) How many subscribers will discontinue after an increase of Rs. $x$ in annual fee ? (ii) If $R(x)$ denotes the total revenue collected after the increase of Rs. $x$ in subscription fee, express $R(x)$ as a function of $x$. (iii)(a) Find the value of $x$ for which $R(x)$ is maximum.  OR  (iii)(b) Find the sub-intervals of $(0, 5000)$ in which $R(x)$ is increasing and decreasing.

answer.text: 5000 subscribers at ₹300; fee raised by ₹x, 10 subscribers leave per ₹1 rise. (i) Subscribers discontinuing = 10x. (ii) Revenue R(x) = (5000 − 10x)(300 + x). (iii)(a) R′(x) = 2000 − 20x = 0 ⇒ x = 100; R″(x) = −20 < 0 ⇒ R is maximum at x = 100. [OR (iii)(b) R′(x) > 0 on (0,100) so R is increasing on (0,100]; R′(x) < 0 on (100,5000) so R is decreasing on [100,5000).]

questions.text: Find the absolute maximum value of $f(x) = \cos x + \sin^2 x$, $x \in [0, \pi]$.

answer.text: f(x) = cos x + sin²x on [0,π]. f′(x) = −sin x + 2 sin x cos x = sin x(2cos x − 1) = 0 ⇒ sin x = 0 or cos x = 1/2 ⇒ x = π/3. f(0) = 1, f(π/3) = 5/4, f(π) = −1. Absolute maximum value = 5/4.

questions.text: If the volume of a solid hemisphere increases at a uniform rate, prove that its surface area varies inversely as its radius.

answer.text: Solid hemisphere: V = (2/3)πr³ increases uniformly ⇒ dV/dt = 2πr²·dr/dt = C (constant) ⇒ dr/dt = C/(2πr²). Surface area S = 3πr² ⇒ dS/dt = 6πr·dr/dt = 6πr·C/(2πr²) = 3C/r ∝ 1/r. Hence S varies inversely as the radius.

questions.text: Find the sub intervals in which $f(x) = \cot^{-1}(\sin x + \cos x)$, $x \in (0, \pi)$ is increasing and decreasing.

answer.text: f(x) = cot⁻¹(sin x + cos x), x ∈ (0,π). f′(x) = (sin x − cos x)/(1 + (sin x + cos x)²). f′(x) = 0 ⇒ sin x = cos x ⇒ x = π/4. f′(x) < 0 on (0, π/4) ⇒ f decreasing on (0, π/4); f′(x) > 0 on (π/4, π) ⇒ f increasing on (π/4, π).

questions.text: A rectangle of perimeter 36 cm is revolved around one of its sides to sweep out a cylinder of maximum volume. Find the dimensions of the rectangle.

answer.text: Rectangle of perimeter 36 has sides x and (18−x); revolving about the side (18−x) makes x the cylinder radius: V = πx²(18−x) = π(18x² − x³). dV/dx = π(36x − 3x²) = 0 ⇒ x = 12 (x ≠ 0); V″ = π(36 − 6x) = −36π < 0 at x = 12 ⇒ maximum. Dimensions of the rectangle: 12 cm and 6 cm.

questions.text: The rate of change of volume of a sphere with respect to its diameter, when its radius is 5 cm, is :

questions.text: Find the sub-interval(s) of $\left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ in which $f(x) = \tan x - 4x$ is increasing.

answer.text: f(x) = tan x − 4x on (0, π/2). f′(x) = sec²x − 4 = 0 ⇒ sec²x = 4 ⇒ cos x = 1/2 ⇒ x = π/3. f′ > 0 for x > π/3, so f is increasing on (π/3, π/2).

questions.text: As shown in the figure below, two vertical electric poles of heights 22 m and 16 m stand facing each other on either side of a 20 m wide road. From a point R on the road, which is at a distance of $x$ m from the shorter pole, two ladders $l_1$ and $l_2$ of certain lengths are placed reaching the tops of the poles. Based on the above information, answer the following questions : (i) Express $p(x) = l_1 + l_2$ in terms of $x$. (ii) Find $p'(x)$. (iii)(a) Find the value of $x$ for which $l_1^2 + l_2^2$ is minimum.  OR  (iii)(b) If the 22 m long pole is also replaced by a 16 m long pole, at what distance from either pole should the ladders be kept so that the sum of squares of lengths of ladders needed to reach the top of the pole is minimum ?

answer.text: Poles 22 m and 16 m on opposite sides of a 20 m road; ladders from R at distance x from the smaller pole. (i) p(x) = l₁ + l₂ = √(22²+(20−x)²) + √(16²+x²) = √(x²−40x+884) + √(x²+256). (ii) p′(x) = (x−20)/√(x²−40x+884) + x/√(x²+256). (iii)(a) Minimise q(x) = l₁²+l₂² = 2x²−40x+1140; q′(x) = 4x−40 = 0 ⇒ x = 10; q″ = 4 > 0 ⇒ minimum at x = 10. [OR (iii)(b) Both poles 16 m: r(y) = 2y²−40y+912, r′(y) = 4y−40 = 0 ⇒ y = 10; r″ = 4 > 0 ⇒ ladders kept 10 m from each pole.]

questions.text: The surface area of a sphere when its volume changes at the same rate as its radius is :

questions.text: Find the values of $x$ for which $f(x) = x^x$, $x > 0$ is increasing.

answer.text: f(x) = xˣ, x > 0. f′(x) = xˣ(1 + log x). Since xˣ > 0, f′(x) = 0 ⇒ 1 + log x = 0 ⇒ x = 1/e. f′(x) > 0 for x > 1/e, so f is increasing on (1/e, ∞).

questions.text: At a birthday party, children are being served orange juice in conical cups, as shown in the figure. Each cup is 15 cm deep and has a radius 5 cm. The juice is being poured into this cup at a rate of $0\cdot1\ \text{cm}^3/\text{s}$. On the basis of the above information, answer the following questions : (i) Establish a relation between the height $h$ of the juice in the cup and radius $r$ of the surface of the juice in the cup, if the semi-vertical angle of the cone is $\alpha$. (ii) At what rate is the juice level in the cup rising when the juice is 6 cm deep ? (iii)(a) When the juice is 6 cm deep, then find at what rate is the upper surface area of juice increasing ?  OR  (iii)(b) When the juice is 6 cm deep, then find the rate at which the wetted surface area of the cup is increasing.

answer.text: Conical cup R = 5, H = 15, juice poured at dV/dt = 0.1 cm³/s. (i) tan α = r/h = 5/15 = 1/3 ⇒ r = h/3. (ii) V = (1/3)πr²h = (1/27)πh³ ⇒ dV/dt = (1/9)πh²·dh/dt ⇒ at h = 6, dh/dt = 1/(40π) cm/s. (iii)(a) A = πr² = πh²/9 ⇒ dA/dt = (2πh/9)dh/dt = 1/30 cm²/s at h = 6. [OR (iii)(b) Wetted surface S = πrl = √10 πh²/9 ⇒ dS/dt = (2√10 πh/9)dh/dt = √10/30 cm²/s at h = 6.]

questions.text: Absolute minimum value of $f(x) = (x - 2)^2 + 5$ in the interval $[-3, 2]$ is :
Determine the values of $x$ for which $f(x) = \dfrac{x - 3}{x + 1}$, $x \neq -1$ is an increasing function.

answer.text: f(x) = (x−3)/(x+1), x ≠ −1. f′(x) = [(x+1)·1 − (x−3)·1]/(x+1)² = 4/(x+1)² > 0 for all x ≠ −1. Hence f is an increasing function on R − {−1}.

questions.text: A spherical balloon loses its volume due to escape of air from it in such a way that decrease of volume at any instant is proportional to its surface area. Show that the radius is decreasing at a constant rate.

answer.text: V = (4/3)πr³; given dV/dt ∝ surface area ⇒ dV/dt = −k(4πr²), k > 0. But dV/dt = 4πr²·dr/dt, so 4πr²·dr/dt = −4kπr² ⇒ dr/dt = −k, a constant. Hence the radius decreases at a constant rate.

questions.text: A company produces cylindrical tumblers, open from the top. Since they want uniformity in the product, they fix the surface area of the tumblers produced. Based on the above information, answer the following questions : If for a tumbler, V is its volume, $h$ the height and $r$ the radius of the circular base, then : (i) Differentiate its volume with respect to radius of the base, where the surface area is constant. (ii) If the company wants to maximize the volume of each tumbler, then establish a relation between its height and the radius of the base.

answer.text: Open-top cylindrical tumbler, surface area S = 2πrh + πr² fixed. (i) V = πr²h = πr²(S−πr²)/(2πr) = (Sr − πr³)/2 ⇒ dV/dr = (S − 3πr²)/2. (ii) For maximum volume, dV/dr = 0 ⇒ S = 3πr²; d²V/dr² = −3πr < 0 confirms a maximum. Then h = (S − πr²)/(2πr) = (3πr² − πr²)/(2πr) = r, i.e. h = r.

answer.text: Roundabout boundary C₁: x²+y² = 64 (radius 8); pond C₂: x²+y² = 4 (radius 2). (i) Two concentric circles. (ii) C₁: y = ±√(64−x²); C₂: y = ±√(4−x²). questions.text: Camphor is a waxy, colourless solid with strong aroma that evaporates through the process of sublimation, if left in the open at room temperature. A cylindrical camphor tablet whose height is equal to its radius ($r$) evaporates when exposed to air such that the rate of reduction of its volume is proportional to its total surface area. Thus, $\dfrac{dV}{dt} = kS$ is the differential equation, where V is the volume, S is the surface area and $t$ is the time in hours. Based upon the above information, answer the following questions : (i) Write the order and degree of the given differential equation. (ii) Substituting $V = \pi r^3$ and $S = 2\pi r^2$, we get the differential equation $\dfrac{dr}{dt} = \dfrac{2}{3}k$. Solve it, given that $r(0) = 5$ mm. (iii)(a) If it is given that $r = 3$ mm when $t = 1$ hour, find the value of $k$. Hence, find $t$ for $r = 0$ mm.  OR  (iii)(b) If it is given that $r = 1$ mm when $t = 1$ hour, find the value of $k$. Hence, find $t$ for $r = 0$ mm.

answer.text: Cylindrical camphor tablet, height = radius r, dV/dt = kS with V = πr³, S = 2πr². (i) Order = 1, Degree = 1. (ii) 3πr²·dr/dt = k·2πr² ⇒ dr/dt = (2/3)k ⇒ r = (2/3)kt + C; r(0) = 5 ⇒ C = 5, so r = (2/3)kt + 5. (iii)(a) r = 3 at t = 1: 3 = (2/3)k + 5 ⇒ k = −3, so r = −2t + 5; r = 0 ⇒ t = 5/2 = 2.5 hours. [OR (iii)(b) r = 1 at t = 1: 1 = (2/3)k + 5 ⇒ k = −6, so r = −4t + 5; r = 0 ⇒ t = 5/4 = 1.25 hours.]

answer.text: x²·dy/dx = x² + xy + y² ⇒ dy/dx = 1 + (y/x) + (y/x)². Put y = vx ⇒ v + x·dv/dx = 1 + v + v² ⇒ x·dv/dx = 1 + v² ⇒ ∫dv/(1+v²) = ∫dx/x ⇒ tan⁻¹v = log|x| + C ⇒ tan⁻¹(y/x) = log|x| + C.

questions.text: Find the particular solution of the differential equation $xy\dfrac{dy}{dx} = (x + 2)(y + 2)$, given that $y(1) = -1$.
questions.topic: Methods of Solving First Order, First Degree Differential Equations

answer.text: xy·dy/dx = (x+2)(y+2), y(1) = −1. Separate: ∫y/(y+2) dy = ∫(x+2)/x dx ⇒ ∫(1 − 2/(y+2)) dy = ∫(1 + 2/x) dx ⇒ y − 2log|y+2| = x + 2log|x| + C. y(1) = −1 ⇒ C = −2. Particular solution: y − 2log|y+2| = x + 2log|x| − 2.

questions.text: Solve the following differential equation : $x\dfrac{dy}{dx} = y - x\sin^2\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)$, given that $y(1) = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$.
questions.topic: Methods of Solving First Order, First Degree Differential Equations

answer.text: x·dy/dx = y − x sin²(y/x) ⇒ dy/dx = (y/x) − sin²(y/x). Put y/x = v ⇒ v + x·dv/dx = v − sin²v ⇒ x·dv/dx = −sin²v ⇒ −∫cosec²v dv = ∫dx/x ⇒ cot v = log|x| + C ⇒ cot(y/x) = log|x| + C. y(1) = π/6 ⇒ C = √3. Solution: cot(y/x) = log|x| + √3.

questions.text: Find the general solution of the differential equation : $y\log y\dfrac{dx}{dy} + x = \dfrac{2}{y}$.
questions.topic: Methods of Solving First Order, First Degree Differential Equations

answer.text: y log y·dx/dy + x = 2/y ⇒ dx/dy + x/(y log y) = 2/(y² log y). IF = e^{∫dy/(y log y)} = log y. Solution: x·log y = ∫(2/(y² log y))·log y dy = ∫(2/y²) dy = −2/y + C ⇒ x log y = −2/y + C (i.e. xy log y = −2 + Cy).

questions.text: Find a particular solution of the differential equation $(x + 1)\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2e^{-y} - 1$, given that $y = 0$ when $x = 0$.
questions.topic: Methods of Solving First Order, First Degree Differential Equations

answer.text: (x+1)dy/dx = 2e⁻ʸ − 1 ⇒ ∫eʸ/(2−eʸ) dy = ∫dx/(x+1). Put 2 − eʸ = t ⇒ −∫dt/t = log|x+1| ⇒ −log|t| = log|x+1| − log|c| ⇒ (x+1)(2−eʸ) = c. y = 0 at x = 0 ⇒ c = 1. Particular solution: (x+1)(2 − eʸ) = 1.

questions.text: Solve the differential equation $y\,e^y\,dx = (y^3 + 2x\,e^y)\,dy$, when $y(0) = 1$.
questions.topic: Methods of Solving First Order, First Degree Differential Equations

answer.text: ye^y dx = (y³ + 2xe^y)dy ⇒ dx/dy − (2/y)x = y²e^{−y}. IF = e^{∫(−2/y)dy} = 1/y². Solution: x·(1/y²) = ∫(1/y²)y²e^{−y} dy = −e^{−y} + c ⇒ x = y²(−e^{−y} + c). At x = 0, y = 1: 0 = −e^{−1} + c ⇒ c = e^{−1}. Particular solution: x = y²(e^{−1} − e^{−y}).

questions.text: Find the general solution of the differential equation $(x^3 - 3xy^2)\,dx = (y^3 - 3x^2y)\,dy$.
questions.topic: Methods of Solving First Order, First Degree Differential Equations

answer.text: (x³ − 3xy²)dx = (y³ − 3x²y)dy ⇒ dy/dx = (x³−3xy²)/(y³−3x²y). Homogeneous; put y = vx ⇒ ∫(3v−v³)/(v⁴−1) dv = ∫dx/x ⇒ (3/4)log|(v²−1)/(v²+1)| − (1/4)log|v⁴−1| = log x + c. Back-substituting v = y/x: (3/4)log|(y²−x²)/(y²+x²)| − (1/4)log|(y⁴−x⁴)/x⁴| = log x + c.

answer.text: Line A l₁: (x−2)/3 = (y+1)/−2 = (z−3)/4 (drs ⟨3,−2,4⟩); Line B l₂: (x−1)/2 = (y−3)/1 = (z+2)/−3 (drs ⟨2,1,−3⟩). (i) The drs are not proportional, so l₁ and l₂ are not parallel. Based on the test attempted by the students, the teacher concludes that 40% of the students have the misconception in the concept of decimal comparison and the rest do not have the misconception. 80% of the students having misconception answered Bijoy as the correct answer in the paper. 90% of the students who are identified with not having misconception, did not answer Bijoy as their answer. answer.text: E₁: student has misconception (40%), E₂: no misconception (60%); A: answers 'Bijoy'. P(A|E₁) = 80/100, P(A|E₂) = 10/100. (i) P(answers Bijoy | no misconception) = P(A|E₂) = 10/100 = 1/10. (ii) P(A) = (40/100)(80/100) + (60/100)(10/100) = 38/100 = 19/50. (iii)(a) By Bayes, P(misconception | Bijoy) = [(40/100)(80/100)]/(38/100) = 16/19. [OR (iii)(b) P(no misconception | Bijoy) = [(60/100)(10/100)]/(38/100) = 3/19.]

In a school, the probability of holding a debate competition is $\dfrac{1}{3}$ and that of a quiz competition is $\dfrac{2}{3}$. In the two participating teams, A has 4 girls and 6 boys and B has 7 girls and 3 boys. If a debate competition is held, the students are selected from team A and for the quiz competition they are selected from team B. If only two students are to be chosen from the teams, then find the probability that one will be a girl and the other a boy.

answer.text: P(debate D) = 1/3, P(quiz Q) = 2/3. Team A: 4 girls, 6 boys; Team B: 7 girls, 3 boys; two students chosen, E = one girl and one boy. P(E|D) = 2·(4/10)(6/9) = 8/15, P(E|Q) = 2·(7/10)(3/9) = 7/15. P(E) = (1/3)(8/15) + (2/3)(7/15) = 22/45.

A box contains 6 cards numbered 1 to 6. A student is asked to pick up two cards, one by one after replacement and note down the numbers on the cards. Let A be the event of getting sum of the numbers on two cards as 10, and B, the event of a number other than 4 on the first card selected. Find $P(A \text{ and } B)$ and find whether the events A and B are independent events or not.

answer.text: Cards 1–6, two drawn with replacement. A: sum = 10 = {(4,6),(6,4),(5,5)}, n(A) = 3; B: first card ≠ 4, n(B) = 30. A∩B = {(6,4),(5,5)}, n = 2 ⇒ P(A∩B) = 2/36 = 1/18. P(A) = 3/36 = 1/12, P(B) = 30/36 = 5/6; P(A)·P(B) = 5/72 ≠ 1/18. Hence A and B are not independent.

questions.text: There are three types of vaccines $A_1$, $A_2$, $A_3$, available in the market to protect the population of the country from spread of certain infection.
